To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the impacts of crisis events on tourism are not equal, and the impacts are influenced by the type and characteristics of crisis events, the characteristics of the destination and the characteristics of tourists.

crisis event type and other causal factors have different impacts on Chinese outbound tourism to Japan and South Korean destinations, and the factors intensifying negative impacts and contributing to post-event recovery and growth differ by destination and event type.

the impact of a political crisis event is greater than the impact of a natural disaster event, the impact of a financial crisis is greater than the economic impact of an economic recession, and that the impact of an environmental disaster event is greater than that of a natural disaster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of crisis events on outbound tourism and the factors influencing this impact.
the negative impact of crisis events on tourism and how to mitigate such impacts, and the positive impacts of crisis events and how to leverage such opportunities for post-crisis tourism development.
crisis event impacts on tourism flows and post-events growth, and the results provide a framework for the development of post-events growth scheme.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the impact of crisis events on tourism is complex and multifactorial.

the negative impact of a crisis event is determined by a number of factors, such as event type, event severity and the extent of the event, the level of media coverage, the extent of the damage, the level of government response, and the extent to which the event affects the tourism industry, and the level of tourist confidence.

the impacts of crisis events on tourist flow from China to Japan or South Korea are complex and varied, but the negative impacts can be alleviated and post-event growth can be achieved through a range of strategies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the negative impacts caused by crisis events are not permanent and that the tourism industry has the potential to recover and grow.
crisis events have a negative impact on tourism, but the impact varies depending on the type and other causation factors.

the impact of crisis events on outbound tourism flows is a complex phenomenon and the impact varies depending on event type, the severity of the event and the characteristics of the tourist destination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the impact of crisis events on tourist flows can be positive, negative or even neutral.

tourism is a resilient industry that can bounce back from crisis events and grow in the post-events period, but only if relevant stakeholders are prepared to take the right measures to mitigate negative impacts and to take advantage of the positive impacts of crisis events to stimulate tourism growth.

tourism recovery and post-events growth is possible and that tourism stakeholders should not be discouraged from investing in tourism recovery and growth schemes after negative impacts of crisis events.
